questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver who operates a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. Examples include drivers who have not scraped ice off windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not familiar with limited rear visibility.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, when will the valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi
When the trailer starts to jackknife
When wheels regain traction after a skid
When air pressure is above 45 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Exercise helps a person become sober after drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol from the body at a fixed rate. Exercise, cold showers, and other tricks do not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose grip on the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose grip on the road
questions.explanation: Skids happen when tires lose traction with the road. This can be caused by braking too hard, accelerating too fast, turning too sharply, or driving too fast.

questions.question: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should rise to normal level within seconds after the engine starts. Do not drive if oil pressure is too low.

questions.question: Carrying liquids in a leaking tank:

options.text: Is safe if it is raining
Is allowed if you are behind schedule

questions.explanation: Leaks are the most important thing to check when inspecting any tank. Transporting gas or liquid in a leaking tank is illegal.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch. All tires must be the same size, not cracked, have correct air pressure, and be in good condition.

questions.question: Surge occurs with which type of cargo?
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles carrying liquid cargo experience surge. Surge is when liquid sloshes from one end or side of the tank to the other, causing dangerous handling problems.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Mirror checks are especially important when turning, changing lanes, merging, and performing tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp. If there is no ramp, find another place to stop such as an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: You are driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph. What is your minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: For speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly and steadily. This helps your vehicle stop smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Your vehicle is hydroplaning. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, slow down by releasing the accelerator and pushing in the clutch.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: Check that your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives. How should you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the road and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: Use reflective triangles or red electric lights when your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives. Never use flares or burning signals with explosives.

questions.question: Baffled tanks:

options.text: Need to be inspected by an electrician.
Let liquid cargo flow through the tank.
Control the temperature of liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let liquid cargo flow through the tank.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have dividers with holes in them. These dividers reduce front-to-back movement while allowing liquid to flow through the entire tank.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move left if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, drivers must leave the lane next to it if possible. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Baffled tanks:

options.text: Are damaged and should not be used.
Reduce liquid surge while allowing liquids to flow through the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce liquid surge while allowing liquids to flow through the tank.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have dividers with holes that let liquid flow through. This reduces front-to-back surge but does not stop side-to-side surge.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Create more space ahead of your vehicle so the tailgating driver can pass. Do not speed up, as this may cause them to continue tailgating at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Are blocked from moisture and cannot freeze.
Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery even after ice has melted on other parts of the road.
